Visual Studio Code 1.141.1 Security Update Closes Critical 9.6 RCE

## Visual Studio Code 1.141.1 Security Update Closes Critical 9.6 RCE

 Software 45027 Published 2026-10-14 07:49 by Philipp Esselbach

 Visual Studio Code 1.141 shipped on October 7, 2026, transforming the editor into an AI agent control center with a unified Copilot harness, a session grid, cross-app handoffs, and cross-platform sandboxing. Microsoft followed up just six days later with Update 1.141.1, a security patch that closes two path-traversal vulnerabilities, including a Critical 9.6 remote code execution flaw (CVE-2026-102238). That RCE requires user interaction to exploit and shows no signs of wild use, but it affects every version from 1.0.0 through 1.141.0. Microsoft recommends upgrading to 1.141.1 immediately and reviewing your sandbox settings before handing agents broad access to files and the network. 

### Visual Studio Code 1.141 turns your editor into an agent control center, then 1.141.1 seals the doors

The Visual Studio Code 1.141.1 security update closed two path traversal vulnerabilities, including a "Critical" 9.6 RCE that needs user interaction to exploit. 

Visual Studio Code 1.141 shipped to the Stable channel on October 7, 2026, and the release notes read less like an editor update and more like a thesis on the future of coding. Microsoft is consolidating everything around AI agents: a unified Copilot harness, sessions you can drag into grids, and the ability to continue work across apps without a reload. The text editor is becoming a control plane.

Exactly six days later, on October 13, Microsoft issued Update 1.141.1. It's a security patch, and it's not a small one. It closes two vulnerabilities, including a "Critical" 9.6 remote code execution flaw. That gap between the two dates isn't a coincidence. Bigger agent capabilities mean a bigger surface to worry about.

#### An editor for agents, not just code

The single most important change in 1.141 is the Copilot harness, now running in a dedicated agent host process built on the Agent Host Protocol (AHP). The point is that the same session can be connected to from multiple VS Code windows at once. It lines up with the standalone GitHub Copilot app and the Copilot CLI, both also powered by the Copilot SDK.

For those running with experiments enabled, this Copilot harness is quietly becoming the default.

Microsoft's headline act is session management. The Agents window now has a two-dimensional grid where you can drag conversations into horizontal or vertical splits and resize the panes. It sounds fiddly until you're juggling three related threads and wish you could see them all at once.

Then there's continuity. Sessions started in the Copilot CLI or the GitHub Copilot app are now picked up automatically as external sessions the moment the first request goes out, even if the Agents window is already open. A similar handoff lets you grab a Codex chat from the ChatGPT app or Codex CLI and finish it in VS Code, history intact, bouncing back and forth between the two.

There's also a worktree cleanup tool, since abandoned agent sessions leave behind isolated Git worktrees that slowly eat your disk. "Chat: Open Worktree Cleanup" shows you how much space inactive sessions are hogging, lets you filter by inactivity and size, and deletes what you don't need. You can set it to run automatically.

For what it's worth, there's still a chat pet. Type /vscode-pet to meet Blobby.

#### The 1.141.1 patch

Microsoft framed 1.141 around six features. The 1.141.1 patch, by contrast, came through a single squashed fix that hardened several security boundaries at once. Path traversal, sandbox configuration, workspace trust, terminal notifications, edit approvals. Forty-two files changed.

Two bugs made it into an actual advisory.

### VS Code 1.141 Brings Copilot, Codex Sessions Together, Tightens AI Agent Security
* By David Ramel
* 10/13/2026
### Key Takeaways
* VS Code 1.141 lets developers continue local GitHub Copilot and OpenAI Codex conversations started in other applications.
* New agent management features include session grids, worktree cleanup, background shell monitoring and expanded sandboxing.
* The release also adds support for multiple GitHub Enterprise instances, new editor controls and experimental development environments.
Microsoft continues to build out Visual Studio Code as a home for AI coding agents, with the latest update making it easier to move between GitHub Copilot and OpenAI Codex, manage multiple agent sessions and control what those agents can access.
VS Code 1.141, released Oct. 7, brings another round of improvements to the Agents window, including better ways to monitor agent activity, reclaim disk space from old sessions and work with agents across different applications.
There's also more sandboxing for AI agents, support for signing in to multiple GitHub Enterprise instances and some traditional editor improvements that have nothing to do with AI.
**Copilot and Codex, Under One Roof**
One of the more interesting changes is the ability to pick up AI coding conversations started outside VS Code without losing the conversation history.
For GitHub Copilot, new conversations started in the Copilot CLI or standalone GitHub Copilot app now automatically appear in the VS Code Agents window after the first request. Developers can open those sessions and continue working without reloading the window.
OpenAI Codex gets similar treatment. Developers can start a chat in the ChatGPT app or Codex CLI, then pick it up in VS Code on the same machine, with the conversation history intact. They can also switch back to the original application later.
There's one restriction: Only one application can send messages to the conversation at a time. If the chat is still open in ChatGPT or Codex CLI, VS Code displays a notification explaining why it can't send messages. Developers need to close the original session before continuing in VS Code.
Interestingly, Microsoft also points out that developers can select a Copilot model in VS Code to keep working with their GitHub Copilot subscription after reaching a ChatGPT usage limit.
**More Ways to Manage AI Agents**
The Agents window is getting more attention as developers increasingly work with multiple AI coding sessions rather than a single chat conversation.
A new grid layout lets developers arrange sessions side by side, split them horizontally or vertically and resize the panes. That makes it easier to compare results or keep an eye on long-running tasks without constantly switching conversations.
Session filtering is also more flexible, with options to filter by execution environment, agent harness or the application that originally created the session.

## Story

GitHub Copilot in VS Code, September 2026 releases - GitHub Changelog

 October 1, 2026 • 2 minute read 

# GitHub Copilot in VS Code, September 2026 releases

This changelog covers VS Code v1.136 through v1.140, shipped throughout September 2026.

September’s releases streamline agent-driven development from implementation through pull request merge. Automations handle repeatable tasks, agent merge helps land changes, and improved session management keeps work organized.

Agents are also more flexible across workspaces, Dev Containers, and apps, while GitHub context helps you collaborate without breaking your flow.

## Agents window

Agents window updates made it easier to automate work, manage sessions, and move changes from implementation to merge.

- Let HydraFusion coordinate models: If eligible, enable preview features and select HydraFusion in the model picker to choose models and workflows for your coding tasks automatically. This feature is in research preview. 
- Schedule recurring work: Use automations to run tasks on an hourly, daily, or weekly schedule or run them on demand. Start from a template or use your own prompt. This feature is in preview.
- Get pull requests ready to merge: Enable agent merge in an active session to let the agent handle review feedback, failed checks, merge conflicts, and workflow reruns. This feature is in preview.
- Create pull requests from agent sessions: Open the pull request form from a Copilot, Claude, or Codex agent session in the Agents window to review and edit the title and description, choose draft and merge options, and create the pull request.
- Navigate related chats and sessions: Agents can now decide to create new chats or sessions. Easily switch to the source chat with the navigation link, or use the sessions list to view all related chats organized in a hierarchical view.
- Keep completed sessions organized: Use Mark as Done suggestions after a session’s pull requests merge, or configure automatic cleanup to keep your session list manageable. This feature is in preview.
- See when sessions need attention: Enable the application badge to surface new results, input requests, and pull request checks on your dock, launcher, or taskbar. This feature is in preview.
- Start Dev Container sessions from the Agents window: Select Use Dev Container from a local or remote folder’s menu to run an agent session with your project’s configured tools and dependencies, including on SSH, Tunnel, and WSL hosts.

## Workspaces and environments

Workspace and environment updates make it easier to continue conversations with the project context agents need.

- Continue quick chats in a workspace: Start a general Copilot chat without a workspace, then attach a local folder when you want to make the conversation specific to that project. 
- Continue Codex work across apps: Pick up a Codex conversation from the ChatGPT app in VS Code and start working on your codebase without copying and pasting context or files.

## Chat and integrations

Chat updates keep agent conversations flowing and make it easier to bring in GitHub context.

- Keep active chats uninterrupted: When an agent sends a message to an ongoing chat, it no longer interrupts the active turn. 
- Attach GitHub context to any chat: Add a GitHub issue or pull request from Add Context, or paste its URL into the new-session input.

Browse the full release notes for VS Code 1.136, 1.137, 1.138, 1.139, and 1.140 to explore everything that’s new.

Download the latest version of VS Code and, as always, happy coding!

### Scalar and Batch Unity Catalog Python UDFs are now generally available

Scalar and Batch Unity Catalog Python UDFs are now generally available on all supported compute types. This release adds named handlers for row-at-a-time scalar UDFs, removes the five-UDF-call-per-query limit, and aligns scalar TIMESTAMP inputs with PySpark behavior.

### Non-deterministic aggregate functions are supported with dynamic table incremental refresh (General availability)

For incremental refresh, these functions are supported only in the SELECT clause. any value remains unsupported.

GitHub Copilot code review now offers additional personal configurations to an expanded set of Copilot plans and an enterprise-level default setting. These improvements are now generally available: A dedicated personal settings page for automatic review and your default review effort An enterprise-wide default review effort setting for organization-owned...

Visual Studio Code 1.140 adds multi-folder sessions - Neowin

# Visual Studio Code 1.140 adds multi-folder sessions 

 Microsoft's latest IDE update brings a new Copilot harness, experimental remote agent delegation, and shared worktree support. 

 Paul Hill Neowin @ziks_99 · Oct 1, 2026 01:22 EDT with 1 comment 

Microsoft has just released Visual Studio Code 1.140, this week it has six release highlights, which is more than last week. Yes, in this update we see expanded agent workflows, improved worktree reuse, and more enterprise AI controls.

The first thing we get this week is the Copilot harness. This adds new agent functionality to VS Code, while keeping your workflow familiar. It is powered by the Copilot SDK, so its behavior and capabilities are consistent with other Copilot products, including the GitHub Copilot app and the Copilot CLI. To use the Copilot harness, select it from the harness picker in the chat input - it may already even be the default choice.

Next up, this version brings experimental support for multi-folder sessions that let you coordinate related work across repositories or isolated worktrees in one session. Prior to this release, every chat within a multi-chat session shared the same folder and checkout, but now each chat can use its own folder or worktree without changes leaking into other chats.

Another experimental feature landing in this update is the ability to delegate tasks to remote agent hosts from the Agents window, without you selecting a host in a picker for each task. Microsoft notes that sessions do not have a workspace unless you specify one. To enable this feature, toggle the setting chat.remoteAgentHostsEnabled.

Other notable features in this update include:

- HydraFusion (Research Preview): Let multiple models draft, critique, and revise coding tasks without coordinating them yourself.
- Shared worktree folders (Experimental): Avoid repeated dependency installs and duplicated artifacts by reusing ignored folders across worktrees.
- Enterprise controls: Ensure everyone in your org follows AI version requirements and defaults.

Within the enterprise controls is the ability to set a default Auto tier. This allows the Auto model in VS Code to operate in different tiers, optimizing for efficiency, balance, or intelligence. Admins can select the default tier, without limiting developers choosing another tier.

The update is ready now, just open VS Code and you will be notified about the update. You can also download it from the VS Code website.

VS Code 1.140: Copilot Harness, HydraFusion & More | Pandromeda

# VS Code 1.140: What's New, Copilot Harness and How to Update

VS Code 1.140 brings a shared Copilot harness, an experimental HydraFusion model orchestrator, multi-folder agent sessions, and remote delegation.

Felix Moreau Staff Software & Guides Editor · 1 Oct 2026 · 9 min read

VS Code 1.140 release highlights. Image: Microsoft.

Visual Studio Code 1.140 is out, and the headline change is a shared "harness" that now runs Copilot's agent the same way inside the editor, in the standalone GitHub Copilot app, and in the Copilot CLI. Microsoft's release also adds an experimental multi-model orchestration system called HydraFusion, experimental multi-folder agent sessions, experimental remote task delegation to other machines, and experimental worktree folder sharing to cut down on duplicate dependency installs.

VS Code 1.140 at a glance

- Released: September 30, 2026
- Headline feature: Copilot harness — one shared agent engine for VS Code, the Copilot app, and Copilot CLI
- Research preview: HydraFusion, an adaptive multi-model orchestration system
- Experimental: Multi-folder sessions, remote agent delegation, shared worktree folders
- How to get it: Automatic update, or Help > Check for Updates

## What's new in VS Code 1.140

According to Microsoft's official VS Code 1.140 release notes, this release is built almost entirely around agent workflows: how Copilot's agent behaves across Microsoft's different products, how multiple AI models can be coordinated on a single coding task, how one agent session can span more than one repository, and how work can be handed off to a separate, more powerful machine. A handful of smaller changes — an accessibility tweak for confetti animations, sharper terminal text rendering on macOS, and new enterprise controls for OpenTelemetry telemetry — round out the update.

Most of the new agent capabilities are gated behind settings and ship as experimental or preview features rather than defaults, so most users will not see their day-to-day workflow change immediately after installing the update. That pattern is consistent with how Microsoft has rolled out agent tooling in recent VS Code releases: new capabilities typically land behind a flag for a release or two, get refined based on feedback filed against the open-source `microsoft/vscode` repository, and only later graduate to being on by default. Developers who want to try the new features early will need to dig into `settings.json` rather than relying on the Settings editor UI, since several of the toggles described below are intentionally left out of that graphical view while they remain experimental.

## Copilot harness: one agent engine, three Copilot products

The biggest structural change in 1.140 is the Copilot harness, a new way of running Copilot's coding agent inside VS Code. Per Microsoft, the harness "is powered by the Copilot SDK, so its behavior and capabilities are consistent with other Copilot products, including the standalone GitHub Copilot app and the Copilot CLI." In practice, that means the same agent logic and tool set now drives Copilot whether someone is working in the VS Code chat panel, in the separate Copilot desktop app, or from a terminal via the CLI, instead of each surface maintaining its own agent implementation.

The harness runs in a dedicated agent host process built on what Microsoft calls the Agent Host Protocol (AHP), documented in its agent host concepts page. Because the agent lives in its own process rather than inside a single editor window, the same running agent session can be reattached from multiple VS Code windows. Microsoft published a companion blog post on the agent host architecture and a how-to guide for working with the Copilot harness for developers who want the deeper technical picture. Users can pick the Copilot harness from the harness selector in the chat input, and Microsoft notes it may already be the default select

Visual Studio Code 1.139.0 Release: What's Confirmed << Windows Tips :: Gadget Hacks

# Visual Studio Code 1.139.0 Release: What's Confirmed 

 By Gadget Hacks

Sep 23, 2026, 06:03 PM

Oct 1, 2026, 06:04 AM

Microsoft released Visual Studio Code 1.139.0 to the Stable channel on September 23, 2026, replacing the sparse Insiders page that had appeared earlier in the month.

The official VS Code 1.139 release notes now include downloads for Windows, macOS, and Linux, along with a full changelog.

The biggest changes center on agent sessions, remote Dev Containers, and several smaller editor improvements.

Microsoft has already moved its Insiders channel to version 1.140, so 1.139 is no longer an upcoming or preview-only release.

## Visual Studio Code 1.139.0 Is Stable Now

Microsoft labels the release:

Visual Studio Code 1.139

with a release date of September 23, 2026, and provides downloads for 1.139.0.

That clears up the naming distinction that existed while the page was still an Insiders placeholder.

The release-notes page uses 1.139 as the release family, while Microsoft's downloads and GitHub tag use the full 1.139.0 version number.

The Microsoft VS Code GitHub repository also lists 1.139.0 as the latest Stable release.

Users who already have VS Code installed can check for it through the application's normal Check for Updates command.

Anyone who wants features beyond 1.139 can use the separate Insiders channel, which has already moved to version 1.140.

## Remote Dev Container Sessions Expand Beyond Local Projects

One of the largest changes is broader Dev Container support for agent sessions.

VS Code already allowed agents to work inside Dev Containers for local folders.

Version 1.139 extends that capability to projects hosted through:

- SSH
- Remote Tunnels
- WSL

That means an agent can run inside the same containerized development environment as a remotely hosted project instead of requiring a duplicate toolchain on the local machine.

The feature uses:

`chat.agentHost.devContainer.enabled`

inside the Agents Window.

The remote project needs a supported Dev Container configuration, and Docker must be available on the remote host.

Microsoft says the feature is rolling out gradually, so it may not be enabled by default for every user immediately.

Anyone who wants to try it sooner can enable the setting manually.

## Large Agent Session Lists Should Load Faster

Version 1.139 also changes how VS Code builds large agent-session lists.

Instead of opening every individual conversation database each time the list is refreshed, the agent host now keeps lightweight session and chat metadata in a central catalog.

Microsoft says full conversation content remains stored separately inside each session or chat database.

The performance improvement becomes more noticeable as the number of sessions grows.

In Microsoft's test with roughly 645 sessions:

- The first session listing after launch fell from about 1.3 seconds to 0.1 seconds.
- Refreshing the list dropped from about 0.6 seconds to 0.15 seconds.

Microsoft describes those results as roughly 12x faster for the first listing and 4x faster for refreshes.

Those are Microsoft's own development-machine measurements, not a guarantee for every installation.

Users with only a handful of agent sessions should expect a smaller difference.

Existing sessions migrate to the new catalog automatically in the background.

## Agent Session Management Gets More Compact

Microsoft added several smaller changes around session organization.

A new Compact View fits more sessions onscreen by reducing the amount of information shown in each row until the user hovers over or focuses it.

Rows can expand automatically when a session needs input or approval.

Users can also hide empty custom groups and the empty Chats section through the session filter.

Session and nested-chat names can now be changed directly in the list.

- Double-clicking the title.
- Choosi

## How it works

Visual Studio Code does not properly encode or escape output in a way that prevents an attacker from injecting malicious code. An attacker can send a specially crafted network request that causes the application to execute the attacker's code with the privileges of the user running Visual Studio Code.

## Technical details

Improper encoding or escaping of output in Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.
